meta.name: Carrier rules dataset: places where carrier documents disagree
meta.source_policy: Every value comes from the carrier's or the seller's own page or PDF. Each section lists its sources.
meta.units: Lengths in inches, volumes in cubic inches, weights in pounds, divisors in in³/lb or cm³/kg, money in USD.
meta.warning: Carriers change rules, usually in January and July. Check the source before you rely on a value.

a.says: Any fraction of an inch is rounded up to the next-higher inch.

b.says: Round each measurement to the nearest whole inch.

items.we_use: Round up. The Service Guide is the contract document.
items.impact: A 12.3 in side bills as 13 in, not 12 in. On a box near a DIM limit, this adds 1 lb or more.

items.topic: Why there are two DIM divisors

a.says: 139 for Daily Rates and 166 for Retail Rates (by rate type).

b.says: 166 for domestic and 139 for export (by destination).
b.doc: UPS 2026 Rate and Service Guide (Retail Rates)

items.we_use: 139 for Daily Rates, 166 for Retail Rates (domestic).
items.impact: The numbers agree. The reason differs, so a support answer and an invoice can seem to disagree.

a.says: Priority Mail divides the volume of a nonrectangular parcel by 166.

b.says: Ground Advantage (commercial) divides the volume of a nonrectangular parcel by 139.

items.we_use: 166 for Priority Mail, 139 for Ground Advantage. Rectangular parcels use 139 for both.
items.impact: The same tube or bag bills at a different DIM weight with each service.

b.doc: The Postal Store: Priority Mail Flat Rate Small Box

items.we_use: 8 11/16 in. An outside length of 8 1/16 in is shorter than the inside length, so it is a typo.
items.impact: Small. It matters if you check that a box fits in a mailbox or a locker.

items.topic: Size and weight limit of the FedEx Large Box

a.says: 12 3/8 × 3 × 17 1/2 in. One Rate boxes must weigh less than 50 lb.

b.doc: FedEx Large Box (FedEx Dominican Republic site)

items.we_use: The US One Rate values, because the comparator uses US services.
items.impact: 3/8 in of length, and a weight limit of 20 lb or 50 lb, depending on the page.
